newsitem.title: UK: Ladbroke says Q3 profit ahead of last year.
newsitem.headline: Ladbroke says Q3 profit ahead of last year.

text.p: British betting and hotels company Ladbroke Group Plc said on Thursday that profit before tax and exceptional items for the three months to September 30, 1996 was "comfortably ahead" of the third quarter of 1995.
Ladbroke said in a third quarter trading statement that its hotels and betting and gaming divisions were both making satisfactory progress.

Property profits declined significantly but the company said that this was because of its strategy of disposing of its commercial property portfolio. The value of contracts exchanged so far this year amounts to 191 million stg.
The effective tax rate for 1996 is projected to be 25 percent compared to 27 percent in 1995. Net debt has continued to fall since the half year.

Ladbroke issued a profit warning at this stage last year because of difficult trading conditions at its betting and gaming division. It later reported 1995 pre-tax profit of 121.3 million stg, down from 128.5 million in the previous year.
In August, Ladbroke said its first half 1996 pre-tax profit excluding exceptional items rose 29 percent to 72.8 million stg.
It also unveiled plans to reunite the Hilton brand for the first time since 1964 after agreeing an alliance with Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC) of the United States.
HHC owns the Hilton name in the U.S. while Ladbroke holds the rights to it in the rest of the world.
Ladbroke said work was well advanced on the launch with HHC of a joint loyalty programme early next year and on the specification of a new jointly owned hotel reservation system.

It said its Hilton International subsidiary continued to trade well although the rate of growth had been somewhat slower internationally than in the first half. UK hotels remained strong with a further increase in profits but difficult trading conditions persisted in continental Europe.
The betting and gaming division performed strongly compared with the third quarter of 1995 when it was badly hit by competiton from Britain's National Lottery.
Turnover from UK retail betting grew following the introduction of slot machines to betting shops in June and the success of a new game based on the results of the Irish Lottery.

Profits were only slightly down on the 1995 period despite an eight million stg cost incurred when jockey Frankie Dettori rode seven winners at a meeting in Ascot in September. The group's other European retail betting businesses improved their performance.
The North American betting and gaming operations showed a marked improvement while there was a stronger performance from the company's four London casinos.
